messages.author: 064eab1f88170342
messages.subject: Mediation with two IVs
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to run a mediation model with two IVs (mom's coparenting and dad's coparenting).


This is my syntax:

model <- '
# a path
EA ~ a1*momposcoparenting + a2*dadposcoparenting

# b path
AQS12 ~ b*EA

# c path
AQS12 ~ cp1*momposcoparenting

#indirect effects
indirect1 := a1 * b
indirect2 := a2 * b

# total effect
total := cp1 + (a1 * b) + (a2 * b)

momposcoparenting ~~ dadposcoparenting
'

mymodel<- sem(model, data=mydata, se = 'bootstrap', bootstrap = 5000, estimator = 'ML', missing = 'FIML', fixed.x = F)

summary(mymodel, standardized = T, fit.measures=T, rsquare=T)
parameterestimates(mymodel, boot.ci.type = "bca.simple") %>% 
kable()


I keep getting an error message saying that "the optimizer (NLMINB), claimed the model converged, but not all elements of the gradient are (near) zero; the optimizer may not have found a local solution; use check.gradient = FALSE to skip this check." Furthermore, when I try to get the bootstrapped estimates using parameterestimates(), I get a warning that says "extreme order statistics used as endpoints."
Can anyone tell me what these warnings mean? I don't get these warnings when I use listwise deletion (and not ML), or if I separate out the models into two separate mediations where there's only one IV per model.  
Any help would be appreciated. Thank you!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Mediation with two IVs
parts:
Are you missing the other c path?

AQS12 ~ cp2*dadposcoparenting

Does the warning go away if that is in the model?  If cp2 is substantially nonzero, the optimizer might have a hard time finding a solution just by inflating cp1 and the mom-dad covariance.  Especially if you have a case of "inconsistent mediation" (related to suppression).

# total effect
total := cp1 + (a1 * b) + (a2 * b)

Total effect of what?  There isn't a "total effect" of multiple predictors on an outcome
  • The total effect of momposcoparenting would be cp1 + indirect1
  • The total effect of dadposcoparenting would be cp2 + indirect2
I get a warning that says "extreme order statistics used as endpoints... if I separate out the models into two separate mediations where there's only one IV per model.  

Do you include cp2 in the separate model for dad?
